system: You are the lead AI reviewer on a deal team. Read the following PRIMARY due-diligence documents and write a concise summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a recommendation. Connect issues across documents where relevant.

exchanges.user:
Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## Partner DD summary

**Recommendation: proceed only conditionally.** The principal risks are loss of the dominant customer following the acquisition and an unresolved bank covenant breach. Resolve both before committing to an unconditional transaction.

### Key findings and red flags

- **Change-of-control revenue exposure:** Arlen Health contributes **41% of revenue—approximately AUD 7.5m annually** (L03). Despite its five-year renewal, Arlen may terminate for convenience on 90 days’ notice exercised within six months after a supplier change of control, without an early-termination fee (L05). Obtain a binding waiver or amendment before closing; the nominal contract term does not secure this revenue.
- **Confirmed covenant breach; lender position unresolved:** The CFO reported leverage of **2.9x versus a 2.5x limit** at 31 March and said the bank had not been notified as of the 14 April email (L06–L07). Subsequent notification, waiver and current compliance are unverified. Review default and enforcement provisions, obtain a written lender waiver, and confirm facility availability and refinancing plans ahead of its 2027 expiry. Arlen loss could further impair earnings and covenant headroom.
- **Positive trading, but concentrated earnings:** Revenue is AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin (L03). These figures do not establish EBITDA or cash conversion. Validate earnings quality and model the downside from Arlen termination. The possible price-related small-business churn is **tentative, not an established trend**; test cohort data before drawing conclusions (L08).
- **Material data-risk obligations:** Arlen requires Australian data hosting, maintained ISO 27001 certification and 99.9% monthly uptime; data-breach liability is capped at three times annual fees (L05). Verify actual compliance and cloud-contract protections (L11). AUD 10m cyber/PI cover is helpful but may not cover the full contractual exposure; confirm policy scope, exclusions and limits (L09).
- **Other diligence is comparatively straightforward:** Employee IP assignments and permissive open-source licences are positive, subject to compliance checks (L10). CTO and Head of Sales retention letters cover only 12 months; verify their start dates and terms (L04). The lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment, reducing consent risk for a share acquisition, although an asset transfer would require separate analysis (L02).

### Required before signing/closing

Secure **Arlen’s change-of-control waiver and the bank’s covenant waiver**, refresh financial and covenant testing, and verify security compliance and insurance coverage. Confirm the chronology and completeness of board records: the supplied 20 March minutes predate the 31 March covenant test and do not establish how the subsequent breach was handled (L07, L12). If either waiver is unavailable, reassess valuation, financing and whether to proceed.
